meta.audience: The multitude at the temple, and the twelve
meta.location: The temple in the land Bountiful
meta.unit: The sermon at the temple (3 Nephi 12–14)
principles: A law fulfilled in a person

world_behind.title: This is the chapter that diverges most
world_behind.text: Against Matthew 5, forty-five of the forty-eight verses carry a real word change, where 3 Nephi 13 changes eighteen of thirty-four and 3 Nephi 14 twelve of twenty-seven. The three sermon chapters move steadily closer to the King James text as they go.

world_behind.title: The twelve are numbered here and named in chapter 19
world_behind.text: Verse 1 gives their count inside a parenthesis and no names at all. 3 Nephi 19:4 lists all twelve, including Nephi's brother Timothy, whom 3 Nephi 7:19 has him raising from the dead. The sermon opens by pointing at men the record has not yet introduced.

world_behind.title: Two beatitudes precede the Matthew sequence
world_behind.text: Matthew 5:3 opens the list with the poor in spirit. Verses 1 and 2 here first bless those who give heed to the twelve and those who believe on their words without having seen. The opening is fitted to a people who will receive the message second-hand.

world_behind.title: The beatitude additions show against Matthew
world_behind.text: Verse 3 has the poor in spirit "who come unto me" where Matthew 5:3 has only the poor in spirit, and verse 6 fills the hungry "with the Holy Ghost" where Matthew 5:6 leaves the filling unnamed.

world_behind.title: Salt and light are conferred rather than described
world_behind.text: Verses 13 and 14 read "I give unto you to be" where Matthew 5:13 and 14 read "Ye are," and verse 14 makes them the light of this people where Matthew 5:14 says the world. Both changes narrow a general saying onto the twelve standing in front of him.

world_behind.title: The law is fulfilled in the past tense
world_behind.text: Verse 18 says in him it hath all been fulfilled, where Matthew 5:18 has till all be fulfilled. The tense is the whole difference between a promise and a report.

world_behind.title: The coin is Nephite
world_behind.text: Verse 26 has a senine where Matthew 5:26 has a farthing. Alma 11:3 makes a senine a judge's daily wage, which fixes the size of the debt the parable is talking about.

words.text: Those who make peace. The word occurs once in the record and once in the King James Bible, at Matthew 5:9, in the same beatitude.
Taste, and by extension usefulness. It appears twice, here and at 3 Nephi 16:15, and the King James Bible spells it "savour" fifty-four times.
A container for measuring grain, large enough to hide a lamp under. One use here against three in the King James Bible, always in this saying.
A term of contempt, left untranslated. One use here and one at Matthew 5:22, and both leave it in the original.
Treated at Alma 11:3, where it is a measure of gold equal to a judge's daily wage. Matthew 5:26 has a farthing in this position, and verse 26 adds a question about paying one from inside a prison.
With spite and malice. The word turns up once here, and three times in the King James Bible. Verse 44 uses it of the people to be prayed for.

phrases.term: Blessed are ye if ye shall give heed unto the words of these twelve
phrases.text: A beatitude that has no parallel in Matthew. It is addressed to a congregation about its own leaders.

phrases.term: More blessed are they who shall believe in your words
phrases.text: The second addition, and the one aimed past the room. Those who have not seen are ranked above those who have.

phrases.term: Blessed are the poor in spirit who come unto me
phrases.text: Three words Matthew does not have. The condition is attached to the blessing rather than left implied.

phrases.term: They shall be filled with the Holy Ghost
phrases.text: Matthew 5:6 says only that they shall be filled. This verse names what fills them.

phrases.term: I give unto you to be the light of this people
phrases.text: Two changes from Matthew 5:14 in one clause. It is given as a commission, and the scope narrows to this people.

phrases.term: One jot nor one tittle hath not passed away from the law, but in me it hath all been fulfilled
phrases.text: The tense of the fulfilment. Matthew 5:18 looks forward to it; this verse reports it accomplished in the speaker.

phrases.term: Come unto me with a broken heart and a contrite spirit
phrases.text: The offering named in 3 Nephi 9:20 carried into the sermon. Verse 19 calls it the law and the commandments of the Father.

phrases.term: Whosoever is angry with his brother shall be in danger of his judgment
phrases.text: Matthew 5:22 has "without a cause" in this sentence and this verse does not. The exception is absent.

phrases.term: While ye are in prison can ye pay even one senine?
phrases.text: A question added to the saying. The point of the parable is put as something the hearer answers.

phrases.term: Old things are done away, and all things have become new
phrases.text: The sentence 2 Corinthians 5:17 gives of a man in Christ, said here of the law itself.

phrases.term: Be perfect even as I, or your Father who is in heaven is perfect
phrases.text: Matthew 5:48 names only the Father. This verse puts the speaker in the sentence first.

verses.label: v. 1–48
verses.title: The most heavily rewritten quotation in the volume
verses.text: Twenty-four chapters here quote a King James chapter at length. This one changes forty-five of its forty-eight verses, ninety-four per cent, second only to 1 Nephi 20, and it takes a hundred and twenty-seven word-level edits to do it, more than twice as many as any other block. Three verses survive word for word: verse 17, "Think not that I am come to destroy the law or the prophets," and verses 40 and 41, the coat and cloak and the second mile. The one statement about the law that is left untouched is the statement that the law is not being destroyed, and the only two commands left untouched are the two hardest to obey.

verses.label: v. 3–11
verses.title: What was added to the beatitudes
verses.text: Nine blessings run here, and almost every one is altered by the same two small insertions. Eight of them gain an opening and, so the list becomes a single accumulating sentence instead of nine separate declarations. Five of them gain the word all, so "blessed are the meek" becomes "blessed are all the meek." Two gain a condition the King James does not state: the poor in spirit are blessed "who come unto me" (v. 3), and those who hunger and thirst are filled "with the Holy Ghost" (v. 6). One is redirected outright. Matthew blesses the persecuted "for righteousness' sake"; here they are persecuted "for my name's sake" (v. 10).

verses.label: v. 13–14
verses.title: A description turned into a grant
verses.text: The King James verses state two facts about the hearers: "Ye are the salt of the earth," "Ye are the light of the world." Both openings are replaced here with the same eleven words, "Verily, verily, I say unto you, I give unto you to be." Being salt and being light stop being what the crowd already is and become something handed to them in the moment of speaking. The second of the two is also narrowed: the light is not of the world but "of this people," and the same narrowing repeats three verses later, where Matthew's "men" becomes "this people" (v. 16).

verses.label: v. 18–20
verses.title: The law, in the perfect tense
verses.text: Matthew keeps the fulfilment ahead of the hearer: not one jot shall pass "till all be fulfilled." Here it is already done, "one jot nor one tittle hath not passed away from the law, but in me it hath all been fulfilled." The clause "till heaven and earth pass" is gone, and so is the whole saying about being called least or great in the kingdom for breaking or keeping commandments. What stands in its place is a different instruction: believe, repent, "come unto me with a broken heart and a contrite spirit," and then the flat statement "the law is fulfilled." The passage that in Matthew sets a standard to be exceeded becomes a passage announcing something finished.

verses.label: v. 26
verses.title: The coin
verses.text: Matthew's prisoner must pay "the uttermost farthing," a Roman coin. Here he must pay "the uttermost senine," and a question is added that Matthew does not ask: "And while ye are in prison can ye pay even one senine? Verily, verily, I say unto you, Nay." The senine is not a biblical unit. It belongs to the weights and measures set out at Alma 11:3–8, and outside that passage it appears in only two other verses in the whole volume, Alma 30:33 and this one. A currency defined four books earlier is carried into a quotation of Matthew, and the substitution turns a proverb about a small debt into a question with an answer.

verses.label: v. 46–48
verses.title: Old things done away
verses.text: Matthew's argument from the publicans, that loving those who love you earns nothing, is cut entirely. Two sentences replace it: "those things which were of old time, which were under the law, in me are all fulfilled," and "Old things are done away, and all things have become new." The second is Paul's phrasing at 2 Cor. 5:17, arriving in a quotation of Matthew. The chapter then closes on one inserted pronoun. Matthew's "even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect" becomes "even as I, or your Father who is in heaven is perfect," which puts the speaker inside the standard he is setting.

chapter.title: The sermon opens on the twelve
chapter.text: Two beatitudes precede Matthew's list, both about receiving the words of those just called. The congregation is addressed before the virtues are.

chapter.title: The unseeing are ranked above the seeing
chapter.text: Verse 2 calls them more blessed. The room had just touched his hands and side.

chapter.title: Salt and light are conferred
chapter.text: "I give unto you to be" changes an observation into a commission. The difference from Matthew 5:13 is one clause and considerable.

chapter.title: The fulfilment is reported as done
chapter.text: Verse 18 puts in the past what Matthew 5:18 places in the future. The speaker is standing where the change happened.

chapter.title: The exception for anger is absent
chapter.text: Matthew 5:22 allows anger with a cause; this verse does not mention one. The saying is tightened.

chapter.title: The parable is priced in local money
chapter.text: A senine, defined at Alma 11:3 as a day's wage for a judge, replaces the farthing, and a question is added that the hearer must answer.

chapter.title: A commandment is added at the heart level
chapter.text: Verse 29 tells them not to let these things enter the heart at all, which is a step before the acts named around it.

chapter.title: The chapter ends with the speaker in the standard
chapter.text: Verse 48 names him alongside the Father. Moroni 10:32 will describe being made perfect in Christ.

applications.title: Notice what was added to the blessing
applications.text: The beatitude here reads "blessed are the poor in spirit who come unto me," where Matthew 5:3 stops at "in spirit." The clause turns a condition into a movement. When you find yourself qualifying for a promise by circumstance alone, look for the step it expects you to take.

applications.title: Take a blessing as a commission
applications.text: Salt and light are given as descriptions and then immediately as duties. When you are told what you are, ask what that makes you responsible for.

applications.title: Watch the word before the deed
applications.text: Three penalties are named and all three are for speech: anger, "Raca," and "Thou fool." The escalation is entirely verbal. Before auditing what you have done to someone, audit what you have called them.

applications.title: Go first, then come
applications.text: Reconciliation with the brother comes before the offering, and the sequence is not negotiable in the sentence. If something is unresolved with a person, that is the appointment to keep before the devotional one.

applications.title: Settle it early
applications.text: Agree with the adversary while still in the way. Disputes get more expensive the further they travel; deal with the one you are currently carrying before it reaches anyone with authority over you.

applications.title: Keep it out rather than fight it off
applications.text: The commandment is to stop the thing at the point of entry rather than at the point of action. Look at where you are currently trying to win a battle that could have been declined earlier.

applications.title: Pray for the specific person
applications.text: Love, bless, do good, and pray for are four separate verbs and the object of all four is an enemy. Name one, and do the fourth this week; it is the only one of the four that costs nothing but honesty.

applications.title: Read the standard as a direction, not a score
applications.text: The instruction is to be perfect "even as I, or your Father who is in heaven is perfect," and it arrives after forty-seven verses of concrete, small, doable things. Take the sentence as naming where the small things point, and go back to the small things.

questions.text: Do I believe more easily because of what I have seen, or despite not seeing?
What have I been given to be that I have been treating as a description?
What anger of mine feels justified enough that I have not looked at it?
Who has aught against me right now?
What am I letting run that would be cheap to settle today?
What am I letting in and then trying to manage?
Who would I have to pray for to obey this verse?

entries.head: 3 Ne. 9:20

anchor.quote: come unto me with a broken heart and a contrite spirit

entries.reason: the same offering named out of the darkness, replacing sacrifice

targets.quote: ye shall offer for a sacrifice unto me a broken heart and a contrite spirit.
targets.verse_text: And ye shall offer for a sacrifice unto me a broken heart and a contrite spirit. And whoso cometh unto me with a broken heart and a contrite spirit, him will I baptize with fire and with the Holy Ghost, even as the Lamanites, because of their faith in me at the time of their conversion, were baptized with fire and with the Holy Ghost, and they knew it not.
targets.markdown: And **ye shall offer for a sacrifice unto me a broken heart and a contrite spirit**. And whoso cometh unto me with a broken heart and a contrite spirit, him will I baptize with fire and with the Holy Ghost, even as the Lamanites, because of their faith in me at the time of their conversion, were baptized with fire and with the Holy Ghost, and they knew it not.
